assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, deliver fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and have changed precision measurement: redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental-constant variation and searches for dark matter. As an experimentalist I value that this is a genuine instrument breakthrough with clear, quantitative, repeatedly demonstrated payoff.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first demonstrated the strontium clock; Ye drove the record accuracy and stability and the many-body clock work. The credited pair is a clean two-person configuration. Other contributors (e.g. Lemonde, Pfund, Hall for the frequency-comb/related infrastructure) are not in the credited names, so I rely only on the supplied strings.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by several groups worldwide (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and others), stable interpretation, and the technology is already in use. Timing is right; the redefinition of the second is still pending, but the science is mature.
uncertainties: Competition between the optical-lattice and trapped-ion clock lineages may complicate how a prize frames the claim.
Hall and Hänsch were recognised in 2005 for the comb; the committee would need to confirm the scope is clearly distinct.
I rely on memory for the detailed priority history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction at the magic angle, followed by the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, opened a vast field (moire materials, twistronics) with very high impact across condensed matter and device physics.
assessment.attribution: Theory (Bistritzer, MacDonald) and experiment (Jarillo-Herrero, with Cao and colleagues; Cao is not in the credited names) form a natural prediction-plus-discovery pairing. The omission of the first author of the 2018 experiments is a real attribution concern, and the supplied credit fits a fair prize only imperfectly; the three credited names are still the most defensible choice.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups and the field is very active, but the nature of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still debated, so the final interpretation is not yet settled. The foundational discoveries are over seven years old and recognition is timely, though the field may still be evolving.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene remains unresolved.
Unfair exclusion of early-career experimentalists and of other theory contributors (e.g. Santos, Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) would need to be weighed.
Sample dependence and twist-angle disorder complicate reproducibility.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube turned a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a neutrino telescope and discovered the diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, followed by evidence for TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068 and neutrinos from the Galactic plane. This opened neutrino astronomy, a core astroparticle-physics achievement and a genuine instrument-driven discovery.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the programme and Karle was a central figure in the detector design and construction; Yoshida contributed to the analysis and the Asian collaboration. The work is a large collaboration, which strains attribution to three people, but Halzen and Karle are the most defensible pair among the supplied names. I note my own field proximity and would rely on the committee for balance.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux confirmed with several channels (muon tracks, cascades, Glashow resonance) and the Galactic plane result in 2023 strengthens the case. Source identification is still emerging at modest significance, but the discovery of the flux is solid and timely.
uncertainties: Individual attribution within a ~300-person collaboration, plus the AMANDA and Baikal/ANTARES/KM3NeT history.
Source-level evidence is only 3-4 sigma for several objects.
Possible perception of conflict because of my own field; I treat the evidence only on the merits.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The localisation of GRB afterglows with BeppoSAX and the optical identification and redshift measurements established the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts, settling a 30-year puzzle and launching modern time-domain high-energy astrophysics. This is a decisive, clearly stated discovery.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX X-ray afterglow detection (Costa et al. 1997); Kulkarni led the optical/radio follow-up. Key contributors such as van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Metzger, Piro and Groot are not among the credited names, so a three-person prize would face a real allocation dispute.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed over 25+ years by Swift, Fermi and gravitational-wave counterparts (GW170817/GRB 170817A); the interpretation is stable. The delay is long but recognition remains valid.
uncertainties: Strong attribution dispute between the space-instrument and ground-based follow-up teams.
Overlap with prior Nobel recognition for related cosmology (accelerating universe) is minimal, but the committee must decide the scope.
My own interest in GRB instrumentation is a potential bias.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics, with strong coupling between superconducting qubits and microwave resonators, provides the architecture for readout and control of nearly all superconducting quantum processors, and has enabled quantum non-demolition measurement and much of quantum-information experiments in the solid state.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed and demonstrated cQED in 2004; four credited names are supplied while a prize allows three. Girvin's theory contribution would be sidelined; the choice of Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf is a judgment call that leaves unresolved allocation.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature technically and independently reproduced, but the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits recognised nearby science, so the committee would need to consider whether a related prize so soon is balanced.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits.
Allocation among four credited names.
Ranking reflects my judgment about balance across fields, not a missing merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays have reported evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, most plausibly from supermassive black-hole binaries, opening a new window on the gravitational-wave spectrum with decades of precision timing.
assessment.attribution: The result rests on multiple large collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, InPTA); the three credited names represent founding and leadership roles but do not capture the many contributors, and the decisive contribution to the claimed detection is spread widely.
assessment.maturity: The 2023 evidence is around 3-4 sigma with Hellings-Downs correlation, with no 5-sigma independent confirmation yet; the astrophysical origin is not settled. This looks premature for now.
uncertainties: Significance below the conventional discovery threshold.
Origin (supermassive black-hole binaries versus new physics) unresolved.
Attribution among multiple collaborations is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller's 1995 proposal of quantum gates with trapped ions, and their later work on quantum simulation and quantum networks, laid theoretical foundations for platforms that have been realised experimentally in ions, atoms and photons.
assessment.attribution: A clean two-person theory configuration. Wineland's experimental ion-trap work was recognised in 2012, and experimental teams (Monroe, Blatt, Wineland) are not in the credited names, so the theory-only framing is the question.
assessment.maturity: Mature: ideas proven by decades of experiments, and quantum computing is advancing. Theory recognition for a platform whose experiments have already been rewarded is arguably timely but may seem secondary.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with the quantum-information theme more broadly.
Whether the committee prefers experimental breakthroughs to theory proposals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry has achieved precision measurements of gravity, the fine-structure constant and the gravitational constant, and underlies inertial sensors and proposed tests of general relativity and gravitational-wave detection. It is an instrument-centred field with clear fundamental and applied impact.
assessment.attribution: Bordé (theory and Ramsey-Bordé interferometer), Pritchard (first atom interferometer with gratings) and Kasevich (with Chu, precision gravimetry) are plausible, but Steven Chu, Jürgen Mlynek and Ernst Rasel are not credited, and priority is spread across several 1991 experiments, so attribution is contested.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have confirmed it and results are reproducible. Long-baseline and space applications are still being developed, so the fundamental-physics payoff is partly pending.
uncertainties: Priority among the 1991 demonstrations and the role of Chu (a prior laureate) complicates the configuration.
Fundamental-physics reach (equivalence principle, gravitational waves) not yet realised.
